steps.what: Locate authoritative sources relevant to the committee assignment
Study subject matters and reconcile conflicting evidence
Discuss difficult subject questions with knowledgeable specialists
Update the existing working brief for later committee preparation

tasks.design: Use native subject folders and a working-brief template in {DOCS}. The legislator reads, tests competing claims and speaks with specialists; the existing brief remains separately authored.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated source navigation and brief headings consume preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source views and document headings can remove those operations without deciding political or technical questions.
tasks.still_hard: Expertise requires understanding contested evidence and recognising its limits.
tasks.human_edge: Ask useful questions and integrate evidence with the committee's actual responsibilities.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated preparation while retaining substantive learning.

reach.task: Explain the strength of subject evidence
reach.learn: Separate established findings from contested interpretation

evidence.claim: Native source folders and brief templates can reduce navigation and repeated structure; the amounts are unmeasured.

assumptions: This case includes a working brief the legislator already reuses for committee preparation. It is not a newly added learning log; if no brief is kept, s4 has no eligible writing baseline.
The legislator chooses remit, topic and source dates in s1 and writes conclusions and open questions in s4; capture and source assessment remain counted. Missing source metadata is checked manually.
Subject views remove 5 of 25 navigation hours; brief headings remove 1 of 10 writing hours. No reduction is assigned to learning or specialist discussion.
External specialist consultation is assumed in s3; internal colleague discussion would use write_internal. Ordinary author saves need no approval.
unknowns: Whether the assumed working brief is used today
research_questions: How much current preparation is repeated navigation or brief structure rather than substantive study?

already_counted.description: Write the legislator's actual conclusions and unresolved questions

incremental.description: Refresh saved subject views when the committee remit changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact questions and information disclosed to the selected specialist; new confidential content requires reconsideration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=94, gross 6 less 1 upkeep gives 5 net. Conservative case: poorly comparable subject collections require all 25 search hours and existing brief headings remove only one writing hour, offset by one upkeep hour. With usable topic metadata retaining 22 source hours and 9 brief hours plus other 65 and 1 upkeep, 3 net remains. Neither scenario reduces study or specialist time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear testimony on bills and public issues

steps.what: Review the issue and locate the relevant submitted testimony
Hear testimony and attend to context, uncertainty and competing interests
Ask witnesses questions to clarify the evidence and its implications
Write working testimony notes used in subsequent deliberation

tasks.design: Use the native hearing-document view and fixed witness/topic headings in {DOCS}. Listening and questioning stay human; the legislator's existing working notes are separately written for later deliberation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated document navigation and note headings add a small burden around testimony.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and fixed headings can remove those operations without summarising away the testimony.
tasks.still_hard: Credibility, lived experience and conflicting interests require direct attention.
tasks.human_edge: Hear people fairly and ask questions that expose missing context.
tasks.altitude: Reduce hearing-document handling while retaining direct engagement.

reach.learn: Distinguish personal working notes from the official hearing record

evidence.claim: Native hearing-document views and fixed note headings can remove repeated setup; no local effect is measured.

assumptions: The legislator already keeps the stated working notes and reads them during deliberation. No new minutes or transcript is added, and clerk labour on the official record is not counted as legislator labour.

The legislator selects agenda item and source revision in s1 and captures witness, claim, qualification and follow-up question in s4. Capture remains counted; ambiguous statements are clarified rather than inferred.
The hearing view removes 1.5 navigation hours; note headings remove 1 writing hour. All 75 listening and questioning hours remain.
Ordinary same-system author saves need no gate. Fixed headings and native views add no recurring administration beyond the retained preparation.
unknowns: Whether working notes are currently structured
research_questions: Do current hearings include the specified repeated navigation and personal note headings?

already_counted.description: Capture the testimony facts and qualifications in working notes

incremental.description: No separate recurring workflow work for fixed headings

approvals.approved_version: The exact question addressed to the witness, reconsidered when the witness or evidential context changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=97.5 and zero upkeep gives 2.5 net. Conservative case: submissions are already directly available and the legislator already uses headings, retaining all 100 hours. A view removing one retrieval hour and headings removing half a writing hour retain 98.5 hours and give 1.5 net. Hearing attendance and questioning remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep abreast of issues affecting constituents

steps.what: Visit constituents and discuss issues in their local setting
Make phone calls to hear constituents' concerns and clarify developments
Locate local newspapers and broadcasts relevant to constituent issues
Read newspapers and view or listen to local broadcasts

tasks.design: Use saved local-source filters in {OTHER}, the existing news-reader application. Retain personal visits, phone calls and direct reading or listening with the legislator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated navigation across local media sources consumes a small portion of awareness work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source filters can reduce navigation without replacing the selected coverage with an automated summary.
tasks.still_hard: Media coverage and unsolicited contacts are incomplete views of constituents' experiences.
tasks.human_edge: Hear concerns directly and recognise perspectives missing from published coverage.
tasks.altitude: Reduce source navigation while preserving direct constituent contact.

reach.learn: Keep source selection broad and avoid mistaking frequency for representativeness

evidence.claim: Native news-reader source filters can reduce repeated navigation without replacing personal contact or reading.

assumptions: The task is awareness through named channels, not a casework transaction. No case log, correspondence response or activity report is added without an existing record and reader.
The legislator selects locality, source and current issue terms in s3, with that work retained. Missing sources are found manually and source coverage is checked there.
Native filters remove 2 of 10 media-navigation hours. None of the contact, reading, viewing or listening time is removed.
The task's calls are explicit external contacts, separately gated. No additional automated alert, message send or capture process is implied.
unknowns: Completeness of saved local source coverage
research_questions: Do filters preserve local viewpoints while removing the assumed navigation work?

already_counted.description: Select coverage and check the scope of the local media sources

incremental.description: Refresh local-source filters as outlets and issues change

approvals.approved_version: The specific statements and disclosures made during the current constituent visit; new personal information requires reconsideration
The verified call recipient and exact statements disclosed on that call; changed recipients or content require a new decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=98, gross 2 less 0.5 upkeep gives 1.5 net. Conservative case: fragmented local broadcasts require almost all navigation, leaving only 0.5 hour removable and offset by 0.5 upkeep. A usable local-source set removing 1.5 navigation hours retains 98.5 hours and 0.5 upkeep gives 1 net. Constituent contact and direct media consumption stay fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain knowledge of national and international events

steps.what: Locate relevant national and international current-events coverage
Read and listen to coverage while checking material claims
Relate current events to existing knowledge and recognise uncertainty

tasks.design: Use saved source and topic views in {OTHER}, the existing news-reader application. The legislator directly reads and checks the coverage and forms an understanding of its significance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated navigation across national and international sources consumes reading preparation time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native source views can reduce navigation without generating a new briefing or choosing the legislator's interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Rapid corrections, competing accounts and missing context require critical reading.
tasks.human_edge: Decide which developments matter and how certain the available information is.
tasks.altitude: Spend less effort finding coverage while retaining direct understanding.

reach.task: Assess the significance of current events
reach.learn: Check primary evidence and recognise incomplete reporting

evidence.claim: Native source and topic views can remove repeated navigation; the proposed savings are unmeasured.

assumptions: Maintaining knowledge does not itself require a report or note. No trailing briefing, approval or publication is introduced without an existing artefact and reader.
The legislator selects topics, sources and dates in s1, with selection and coverage checks counted. Missing or unreliable metadata requires manual navigation.
Saved views remove 4 of 20 navigation hours. Reading, source verification and interpretation remain fully retained, and no automated summary replaces them.
Overlapping source navigation with committee study or local coverage is allocated once on the actual portfolio. No automated notification or external send is implied.
unknowns: How much navigation is already consolidated
Coverage gaps in saved topic views
research_questions: Do native views preserve source diversity and reduce actual navigation rather than reading time?

already_counted.description: Read, verify and interpret the coverage

incremental.description: Maintain topic and source views when coverage changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 central B=100, R=96, gross 4 less 1 upkeep gives 3 net. Conservative case: inconsistent source metadata retains 19 navigation hours, with other 80 and 1 upkeep yielding zero. With usable topic metadata removing 3 navigation hours, 97 hours remain and 1 upkeep gives 2 net. Direct reading and interpretation remain unchanged in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Preserve democratic judgement and direct listening while reducing repeated source and document handling.
reach: Connect committee learning with informed questioning
Maintain direct contact alongside diverse public information
skills_to_grow: Use native document and news views
Keep personal working notes distinct from official records
role.ambitious_version: A legislator who is better prepared for testimony and deliberation without substituting automated summaries for understanding.
